- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to correct for recent high prices, leading to prolonged overestimation.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 5–10 days, then gradually decays but still lags behind true trend.
- Model underreacts to sharp downward moves in history, often failing to anticipate sudden price drops.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the final 5–10 days, especially when true outcomes show a downward correction.
- Model exhibits “lagged” behavior — forecasts are often 1–2 days behind the true price trend, especially after volatility spikes.
- Overestimation is more pronounced when history includes recent high prices; model fails to adjust downward sufficiently.
